THE MURDER OF TSAI TIAO-TU: YANG CHIA-CHU SENTENCED
TO SEVEN YEARS' IMPRISONMENT ON APPEAL

Yang Chia-chu (楊家駒) alias Yang Poo-chen
(楊步辰) alias Siao Yang (小楊), Chief of the General
Affairs Department of the Asia Rehabilitation Society
(兴亚会), Chen Ping (陳平), Chief of the Organization
Department, and Zing Sih-kong (秦錫康), an employee of
the Society, were arrested sometime ago by D.S.I. Wong
Foh-sung (黃福森) of the Shanghai Municipal Police in
connection with the murder of Tsai Tiao-tu (蔡釣徒),
proprietor of the "Social Evening News" (社會晚報). After
trial by the Shanghai First Special District Court, Yang
was sentenced to life imprisonment, while Chen and Zing
were given three years each.
The three accused filed an appeal with the
Second Branch Kiangsu High Court.
On the afternoon of December 14, Presiding
Judge Yoeh (有 ) of the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court
handed down the following decisions:-
The original sentence passed on Yang Chia-
chu by the Shanghai First Special District Court is cancelled.
Yang is sentenced to seven years' imprisonment.
The appeal filed by the accused Chen Ping
and Zing Sih-kong is dismissed.

兴亚会总务处处长杨家驹（楊家駒），又名杨步辰（楊步辰），又名小杨，该会组织处处长陈平（陳平），以及该会职员秦锡康（秦錫康），此前因涉及《社会晚报》业主蔡钓徒（蔡釣徒）被杀一案，被上海公共租界工部局警务处侦探长黄福森（Wong Foh-sung）逮捕。经上海第一特区地方法院审理，杨家驹被判处无期徒刑，陈平和秦锡康各被判三年徒刑。
三名被告向江苏高等法院第二分院提起上诉。
12月14日下午，江苏高等法院第二分院审判长有法官（Yoeh）作出如下判决：
撤销上海第一特区地方法院对杨家驹的原判。
改判杨家驹有期徒刑七年。
驳回被告陈平和秦锡康的上诉。

SEP 1 3 1938
Police Delve Deeper In Case
Involving Yellow Way Gunmen;
Details Of Murders Produced
Prisoners Tell Strange Tales Of Local Plots
Against Anti-Japanese Chinese Leaders;
Japanese Colleagues Now Missing
Killing Of Newspaperman Described
THAT the fatal shot which killed Dr. Herman G. E. Liu, president of the Shanghai University, was fired from one of the 27 pistols sold by the SMP to the Japanese Army Special Service Section was one of the startling revelations recently unearthed by the Settlement authorities with the arrest of four terrorists now in custody, it was learned from authoritative sources today.
At the same time, the motive for the murder of Tsai Tsao-tu, the late proprietor of the Social Evening News, was established by investigators. The newspaper owner was murdered by members of the Huang Hwei or Yellow Society, because he was suspected of being a spy in the employ of the Chinese government.
Poison Fruit Sent
The sending of poisoned fruit to editors of the Morning Leader, a British-owned Chinese daily, was also attributed to the work of the society's hirelings.
These facts were gathered by the police in the course of an exhaustive investigation into the past activities of the four men who will be tried in the First Special District Court for the second time some time this week. In addition to obtaining full confessions from the quartet, the police also discovered a diary written by one of them, which contains valuable information regarding the activities of the terror society.
Face Charges
The four terrorists are Yang Kya-chu, alias Colonel Walter Yang, former chief of the general affairs bureau of the Asia Rehabilitation Society with headquarters at the New Asia Hotel; Zing Sh-kong, another member of the society; Zung Bing, former interpreter in the employ of the society; and Hsu Yuh-ling, a hired bomb-thrower.
The four were charged with aiding and abetting the murder of Tsai Tsao-tu and offences against public order during the last trial held in camera at the court, it was learned today from several sources.
All Took Part
All the four had a hand in the murder of the late publisher. It was disclosed that the actual murder was however, carried out by members of the sister society, the ...
Resume of the Tsai Tsao-tu murder case, based on the confessions made the accused and the diary and documents seized from Colonel Walter Yang, is as follows:
Met Zing
Some time in January, Tsai came to know Zing Sh-kong, who lives in the next house to his home at House 7, Keng Yu Li, off Rue Auguste Boppe in the Concession. Zing introduced Walter Yang to Tsai. At that time Yang was a member of the Asia Rehabilitation Society.
Knowing that Yang was an influential member of the society, Zing requested him to get him a pass in order to visit his factory on Hochien Road in the eastern area. Tsai fostered his friendship with Yang, because he was said to have been anxious to resume the operations of his paper which had been previously suspended by order of the SMC, allegedly because of a protest from the Japanese authorities.
Became Brothers
The three became sworn brothers in the Rainbow Temple on Nanking Road. They were frequently seen together. In due time, all three became trusted friends of one Kimura, Japanese adviser to the Asia Rehabilitation Society.
Of the trio, Yang is the most interesting character. Some 30 years ago, while still in his teens, he obtained a position with a local American law firm through his lawyer father. He was involved in a misappropriation case and fled to Hankow, after destroying evidence by setting fire to the office. He was arrested at Hankow, extradited to Shanghai, and served a term both at the reformatory and the Ward Road Jail.

1938年9月13日
警方深入调查涉及青帮枪手的案件；
披露谋杀细节
囚犯讲述针对抗日中国领导人的本地阴谋奇闻；
日本同伙目前失踪
详述报人被杀经过
据今日从权威渠道获悉，上海大学校长刘恩荣博士（Dr. Herman G. E. Liu）遭致命枪击身亡，而射出致命一枪的手枪，竟是工部局警务处（SMP）出售给日本陆军特务机关的27支手枪之一，这是当局最近逮捕四名目前在押恐怖分子后揭露出的惊人真相之一。
与此同时，调查人员查明了已故《社会晚报》业主蔡钓徒（Tsai Tsao-tu）被杀的动机。这位报业老板是被黄会（Huang Hwei，即青帮）成员杀害的，因为他被怀疑是中国政府雇用的间谍。
寄送毒果
向英资中文日报《晨导报》（Morning Leader）的编辑寄送毒水果一事，也被归咎于该会所雇佣爪牙所为。
这些事实是警方在对这四名男子过去的活动进行详尽调查过程中收集的，他们将于本周内再次在第一特区地方法院受审。除了获得这四人的完整供词外，警方还发现了其中一人写的一本日记，其中包含有关该恐怖社团活动的宝贵信息。
面临指控
这四名恐怖分子分别是：杨家驹（Yang Kya-chu），又名沃尔特·杨上校（Colonel Walter Yang），前兴亚会总务局局长，总部设在新亚酒店；秦锡康（Zing Sh-kong），该会另一名成员；钟炳（Zung Bing，音译），前受雇于该会的翻译；以及徐玉玲（Hsu Yuh-ling，音译），一名受雇的投弹手。
据今日从多方获悉，这四人被控在上次法庭秘密审讯期间协助和教唆谋杀蔡钓徒（Tsai Tsao-tu）以及犯有危害公共秩序罪。
全员参与
四人均参与了杀害这位已故出版商的活动。据披露，实际谋杀行为是由其姊妹社团……的成员实施的。
基于被告供词以及从沃尔特·杨上校处缴获的日记和文件，蔡钓徒谋杀案摘要如下：
结识秦某
一月的某个时候，蔡钓徒结识了住在法租界奥古斯特·博佩路（Rue Auguste Boppe）庚余里7号他家隔壁的秦锡康（Zing Sh-kong）。秦将沃尔特·杨介绍给蔡。当时杨是兴亚会成员。
秦知道杨是该会有影响力的成员，便请求杨帮他弄一张通行证，以便去东区河间路（Hochien Road）的工厂。蔡刻意加强与杨的友谊，因为据说他急于恢复此前因据称受到日本当局抗议而被工部局勒令停刊的报纸业务。
结拜兄弟
三人在南京路的彩虹庙结为异姓兄弟。人们经常看到他们在一起。不久，三人都成了兴亚会日本顾问木村（Kimura）的信任好友。
在这三人中，杨是最有趣的人物。大约30年前，当他还是十几岁的少年时，通过其律师父亲的关系在当地一家美国律师事务所谋得职位。他卷入一起挪用公款案，在放火烧毁办公室销毁证据后逃往汉口。他在汉口被捕，被引渡回上海，并在感化院和华德路监狱服刑。

作为前圣约翰大学学生，他英语讲得很好……没有仆人……受雇于……

A few years later, he saw service in the infamous general Chang Chung-chang's army in Shantung. It was in this warlord's army as an intelligence officer that Yang became a colonel, and ever since then has been known as "Colonel Walter Yang." Later, he was a department head of the intelligence bureau in the Nanking government, in charge of espionage work concerning the activities of Japanese in China.

Became Detective
When he was dismissed from the bureau, he came to Shanghai and joined a local foreign detective bureau as a Chinese secretary. It was at this time that he met Zing Sih-kong. He was dismissed, however, when he was involved in another misappropriation scandal. At the start of the war, he was unemployed. He met on Woo Chia-seng, who was then in close connection with the Japanese, and through the latter he was engaged to draft the regulations and constitution for the Asia Rehabilitation Society, being a former law office clerk. He was later made chairman of the general affairs bureau of the society, drawing $100 a month upon the recommendation of Kimura.

Party Thrown
At this juncture, Tsai popped onto the scene. When Yang was able to get passes for both Zing and Tsai, the latter was elated and gave an elaborate party to the Japanese adviser, one Liu Song, who was then the most influential Chinese member of the society, Zing, and others at the T.T. Restaurant on Kwangse Road and the Crystal Palace Theatre Rue Kraeter. The Japanese and Liu Song declined the invitation, however.
Just after the big party, Kimura is said to have told Yang that Tsai was a Chinese spy and that he must be detained at the New Asia Hotel at all cost. This information was relayed to Tsai, who the next day showed a document to Liu Song, which was supposed to have been issued by General Yang Hu, then garrison commander for the Shanghai-Woosung area, ordering the suspension of the Social Evening News. It is believed that the showing of the said document was the cause of further suspicion and his subsequent death.

Goes To Hotel
On February 5, both Tsai and Zing was ordered to report at the New Asia Hotel. Tsai took his car as far as the bridge where he was stopped by the Japanese sentries because the driver had no pass. That was the last the driver saw of his master.
Zing, whose car was taken by Yung, had to go to Hongkew by bus and was delayed at a dinner party given by one Konomi, Japanese adviser to the Huang Tao Hwei. This is what transpired at the party.

Sent Upstairs
Near the close of the dinner, Tsai was ordered to report at a room on the sixth floor of the building by two plain-clothes men. Before he left the table, Tsai is said to have appealed to Liu Song to help him in case of any trouble. Meanwhile, Zing arrived at the hotel to learn of the arrest of Tsai.
Then Tsai's severed head was found near the French Police Station on Route Stanislas Chevalier on February 7. It was disclosed that the head was originally intended to be thrown into the police headquarters, according to a boast allegedly made by Konomi, it was stated by the prisoners. Hsu Tuh-ling, who is the only one of the six terrorists who was not sentenced the other day, washed the head and delivered it to several hired hands who abandoned it in the Concession.

Zing Moved
According to Yang's own confession, he received $50 for his part in luring Tsai to the hotel while Liu Song received $10.39 Zing got scared after the murder and moved to the hotel.
At about this time, Yang lost favor with the Japanese and lost his job for misappropriating society funds. He was arrested at his home on Yates Road in August and Zing's car which he used was located in a repair shop on Weihaiwei Road. Meantime, Zing surrendered himself to the police, but was released when he gave a satisfactory statement. He was, however, re-arrested later when he came to live in the Settlement. It was also disclosed that Zing's concubine, Suzanne Zing, had to work as a dancer in Hongkew when he lost favor with the chief of the society and he was dismissed from the society.

Japanese Transferred
Yang implicated Zung Bing, a former assistant to a Japanese dentist who adopted him. Zung succeeded Yang as the chief of the general affairs bureau of the society. Zung was arrested on August 5 at the Continental Building. At about this time, Konomi was transferred to another post because of a kidnapping scandal. Kimura was also transferred to another post. Liu Song is said to have also lost his job, his place having been taken by one Zang Mo-chiu.
The actual killing of Tsai was done by hired hands under the direction of Zang Yu-ching, 315-pound chief of the Huang Tao mob, and Konomi, the Japanese adviser, according to Yang's confession.

几年后，他在山东臭名昭著的张宗昌将军麾下服役。正是在这位军阀的军队中担任情报军官时，杨晋升为上校，从此被称为“沃尔特·杨上校”。后来，他担任南京政府情报局局长，负责监视在华日本人活动的情报工作。

成为侦探
当他被该局解职后，来到上海，加入当地一家外国侦探社担任中文秘书。正是在这时，他结识了秦锡康（Zing Sih-kong）。然而，当他卷入另一起挪用公款丑闻时又被解雇。战争爆发初期，他处于失业状态。他遇到了当时与日本人关系密切的吴家声（Woo Chia-seng，音译），并通过吴受聘起草兴亚会的规章和章程，因为他曾是律师事务所职员。后来，在木村的推荐下，他被任命为该会总务局局长，月薪100美元。

举办宴会
就在此时，蔡钓徒登场。当杨能为秦和蔡两人弄到通行证时，蔡欣喜若狂，并在广西路（Kwangse Road）的T.T.餐馆和克拉特尔路（Rue Kraeter，音译）的水晶宫大戏院，为日本顾问、当时该会最有影响力的中国成员刘松（Liu Song，音译）、秦等人举办了一场盛大的宴会。然而，日本人和刘松拒绝了邀请。
就在盛大宴会刚结束后，据说木村告诉杨，蔡是中国间谍，必须不惜一切代价将其扣留在新亚酒店。这一消息被透露给蔡，蔡第二天向刘松出示了一份文件，据称是由时任沪淞地区卫戍司令的杨虎将军签发的，命令《社会晚报》停刊。据信，出示该文件导致了进一步的怀疑及其随后的死亡。

前往酒店
2月5日，蔡和秦均被命令到新亚酒店报到。蔡乘车行至桥头时，因司机没有通行证而被日本哨兵拦下。那是司机最后一次见到他的主人。
秦的车被荣（Yung，音译）开走，他不得不乘公共汽车去虹口，并在黄道会（Huang Tao Hwei）日本顾问近藤（Konomi，音译）举办的晚宴上被耽搁。以下是宴会上发生的情况。

被带上楼
晚宴接近尾声时，两名便衣人员命令蔡到该建筑六楼的一个房间报到。据说蔡在离席前曾恳求刘松，万一出事请帮助他。与此同时，秦到达酒店，得知蔡被捕的消息。
随后，2月7日，蔡的头颅在斯塔尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路（Route Stanislas Chevalier，即今淡水路）法国警察局附近被发现。据囚犯称，据近藤吹嘘，这颗头颅原本打算扔进警察总局。徐土林（Hsu Tuh-ling，音译）是六名恐怖分子中唯一前几天未被判刑的人，他清洗了头颅，并将其交给几名雇工，后者将其丢弃在租界内。

秦搬家
根据杨自己的供词，他因引诱蔡去酒店而获得50美元报酬，而刘松获得10.39美元。谋杀发生后秦感到害怕，搬进了酒店。
大约在这个时候，杨因挪用社团资金而失宠于日本人并丢了工作。他于八月在其耶茨路（Yates Road，音译）的家中被捕，他所使用的秦的汽车在威海卫路的一家修理厂被发现。与此同时，秦向警方自首，但在提供令人满意的陈述后被释放。然而，当他搬到租界居住后，后来再次被捕。还披露说，秦的小妾苏珊·秦（Suzanne Zing）在该会会长失宠并被开除出会时，不得不在虹口做舞女谋生。

日本人调职
杨牵连出钟炳（Zung Bing），他是一名日本牙医的养子兼前助手。钟接替杨担任该会总务局局长。钟于8月5日在大陆商场（Continental Building）被捕。大约在这个时候，近藤因一起绑架丑闻被调往其他职位。木村也被调往其他职位。据说刘松也丢了工作，他的位置由臧莫秋（Zang Mo-chiu，音译）取代。
根据杨的供词，蔡的实际杀害是由黄道帮头目、体重315磅的臧玉清（Zang Yu-ching，音译）和日本顾问近藤指挥下的雇凶所为。

据说随着朋友近藤的调职，钟炳切断了与该会的联系。有一次，据说近藤向钟炳吹嘘，一位最坚定的抗日中国领导人“已被干掉”，意指

妾室在场

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

8EP 4 1939

Hwangtao Gang Accused of
Editor's Murder

Responsibility for Severed Head Found in French
Concession Laid to Japanese Terrorist Gang

SENSATIONAL revelations concerning the pro-Japanese terrorist
gang known as the "Hwang Tao" or "Yellow Way" Society
and its associates were made yesterday afternoon in the course
of a three-hour hearing held behind closed doors in the First
Special District Court. The disclosures chiefly served to shed light
on the kidnapping and brutal murder of Mr. Tsai Tiao-tu, editor
of the Chinese newspaper "The Social Evening News," whose
severed head was found on February 6, last, near the French
Concession Police Headquarters in Route Stanislas Chevalier. A
warning in Chinese not to engage in anti-Japanese activities was
pinned to an electric light post above the head. The remainder
of the body was never found.

The facts given below are part of
the evidence offered in court yes-
terday by four Chinese arrested by
the Settlement Police in recent
weeks for complicity in the murder.
Their names are Yang Kya-chu
(alias "Colonel" Walter Yang), Zing
Sih-kong, Hsu Tuh-ling, and Zung
Sih-kong, Hsu Tuh-ling, and all
have various aliases.

The late Mr. Tsai Tiao-tu went
to Hongkew on the forenoon of
February 5 last, in his own motor-
car, and proceeded to the New Asia
Hotel, headquarters of the "Huang
Tao" gang and later of the so-called
"Ta Tao" administration, it was re-
vealed in court yesterday.

He again visited the New Asia on
the evening of February 5, when he
was murdered. On that evening,
Yang Kya-chu and Zing Sih-kong,
according to their testimony, lured
the Chinese editor to the hotel at
the instigation of a Chinese not now
under arrest, and a Japanese named
Konomi, whose present whereabouts
are not known to the police either.
Konomi's name is often mentioned
in "Huang Tao" cases.

"Colonel" Walter Yang, a former
university student, and Chinese Cus-
toms man assistant in an American
lawyer's office in Shanghai, said that
Tsai was taken away from the din-
ner table in the New Asia Hotel
the evening of February 5. It was
about 8 o'clock, and two Japanese
removed Tsai after speaking in
Japanese to the Japanese host at the
gathering. Tsai was not seen again
that night, Yang said. The follow-
ing evening his head was found in
Route Stanislas Chevalier.

Some ten days after the disappear-
ance of Tsai, "Colonel" Yang was
appointed "Chief of the General
Office of the Asia Reconstruction
Society," he revealed. This was a
Japanese-sponsored organization with
quarters in the New Asia Hotel. At
that time Yang said he had fre-
quent dealings with a Japanese

named Kimura at the New Asia.
Kimura being an important "adviser"
to the "Huang Tao" society. Yang
later resigned his post in the or-
ganization.

The testimony of Hsu Tuh-ling,
coolie, who joined the "Huang Tao"
Society because he was out of work,
dealt with the actual production, in
the New Asia Hotel, of Tsai's severed
head on the evening of February 5.
Hsu related how he was awakened
while taking a nap, at 9.30 p.m. on
that day, in a room of the hotel.
A Chinese whom he recognized was
shaking him by the shoulder.

The other man held a pail in his
hand. He instructed Hsu to "wash
the head," according to Hsu's evid-
ence.

Hsu, struggling to get wide-awake,
asked groggily, "What kind of head?"
The answer, Hsu said, was "an
anti-Japanese human head."

Hsu looked into the pail and saw,
truly enough, a human head inside.
It was covered with blood.

Hsu said he would not wash it,
but he was told that if he did not
he would have trouble. After some
persuading he finally agreed to per-
form the gruesome task after switch-
ing off the light in the bathroom.
Two other Chinese helped him. Hsu
was curious and asked Whose head
it was. He said he was told that it
was Tsai's and that it had been
chopped off by "one Konomi."

The coolie testified that he was
not paid anything for washing Tsai's
head but that he heard, at about
March 10, while visiting 86 Jessfield
Road, two other Chinese members
of the "organization" boast that
they had received $5 for the work.
They were the two men who had
helped him do the "job."

After hearing this and much other
testimony, the Judge adjourned the
case yesterday till an unnamed date.

1939年9月4日

黄道帮被控谋杀编辑

法租界发现断头案的责任归咎于日本恐怖团伙

昨天下午，在第一特区法院闭门举行的长达三小时的听证过程中，披露了关于亲日恐怖团伙“黄道”社（Hwang Tao，又称“Yellow Way” Society）及其同伙的惊人真相。这些披露主要阐明了中文报纸《社会晚报》编辑蔡钓徒先生被绑架并惨遭杀害一案，其断头于去年2月6日在斯塔尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路（Route Stanislas Chevalier，即今金陵西路）的法租界警察总部附近被发现。头颅上方的电线杆上钉着一张中文警告标语，告诫人们不得从事反日活动。尸体其余部分至今未被找到。

以下事实是近期被租界警方以谋杀共犯罪名逮捕的四名中国人在昨天法庭上提供的证词的一部分。他们的名字是杨雅初（别名“沃尔特·杨上校”）、Zing Sih-kong、徐笃灵和Zung Sih-kong（注：原文此处重复列出Hsu Tuh-ling及Zung Sih-kong，依原文译出），且均拥有多个别名。

据昨天法庭披露，已故的蔡钓徒先生于去年2月5日上午驾驶自己的汽车前往虹口，并进入新亚酒店，该处是“黄道”帮的总部，也是后来所谓“大道”政府（Ta Tao administration）的所在地。

2月5日晚，他再次造访新亚酒店，并在那里遇害。据杨雅初和Zing Sih-kong的证词，当晚，在一名目前未被逮捕的中国人和一名名叫Konomi的日本人的唆使下，他们将这位中文报纸编辑诱骗至酒店。警方的档案中也不清楚Konomi目前的下落。在“黄道”社的案件中，Konomi的名字经常被提及。

“沃尔特·杨上校”曾是一名大学生，也是上海一家美国律师事务所的中国海关事务助理，他说蔡氏于2月5日晚在新亚酒店的餐桌上被带走。当时大约是8点钟，两名日本人在用日语与聚会的日本主人交谈后，将蔡氏带走。杨称，那晚之后再无人见过蔡氏。次日晚上，他的头颅在斯塔尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路被发现。

蔡氏失踪约十天后，“杨上校”被任命为“亚洲复兴社总办事处主任”，他透露道。这是一个由日本人赞助的组织，办公地点设在新亚酒店。当时杨称他经常与新亚酒店的一位名叫木村（Kimura）的日本人打交道。木村是“黄道”社的重要“顾问”。杨后来辞去了该组织的职务。

苦力徐笃灵的证词涉及2月5日晚在新亚酒店实际处理蔡氏断头的过程，他加入“黄道”社是因为失业。徐叙述了当天晚上9点30分，他在酒店房间打盹时被唤醒的情形。一个他认识的中国人正在摇他的肩膀。

另一个人手里拿着一个桶。根据徐的证词，那人指令徐“把头洗干净”。

徐努力让自己清醒过来，迷迷糊糊地问：“什么头？”
徐说，得到的回答是“一个反日的人头”。

徐往桶里一看，确实里面有一颗人头。上面沾满了鲜血。

徐说他不愿清洗，但被告知如果不洗会有麻烦。经过一番劝说，他最终同意在关掉浴室灯光后执行这项可怕的任务。另外两名中国人协助了他。徐感到好奇，问这是谁的头。他说他被告知那是蔡氏的头，是由“一个叫Konomi的人”砍下的。

这名苦力作证说，清洗蔡氏的头颅并未获得任何报酬，但他听到，大约在3月10日，当他访问杰斯菲尔德路86号（Jessfield Road，即今万航渡路/江苏路一带）时，该“组织”的另外两名中国成员吹嘘他们因这项工作收到了5美元。这两人就是曾协助他完成这项“工作”的人。

在听取了这一证词及许多其他证词后，法官昨天宣布休庭，复庭日期未定。

SEP 10 1938

Konomi, Alias Tanaka, Pictured
As “Brains” of Terrorists
Witness Describes Inner Workings of “Huang Tao”
Society ; Dr. Herman Liu Case Mentioned

IN preparation for the next hearing of the case in the First Special District Court, Settlement detectives yesterday pushed their searching investigation into the reign of terror conducted since early this year by the “Huang Tao” or “Yellow Way” band of pro-Japanese thugs from headquarters on the sixth floor of the New Asia Hotel, Hongkew. The members of the gang who are not now behind bars have scattered, the chief Chinese, Zang Nyoh-tsing, having been given a roving commission away from Shanghai as “garrison commander of the Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow area.”

Another man much wanted by the Settlement Police is a Japanese named Konomi (no first name or initials given), alias Tanaka. This man, who sometimes dressed in Chinese clothes, was “adviser” to the “Huang Tao” Society until the first week of last April, according to testimony given in the Chinese court, where his photograph, together with those of many other members of the organization, was produced and identified by witnesses on Thursday.

Among the important court evidence sifted by detectives yesterday was that given by a young Japanese-speaking Chinese, Zung Bing, or Zung Ziang, who shed strong light on the inner workings of the terroristic society since its inauguration last winter. His story, corroborated by the testimony of several other members of the gang now in custody, reads almost like detective fiction.

Knowledge of Japanese

Zung Bing told the court that he learned to speak Japanese while apprenticed to a Japanese physician in Hongkew and that he visited Japan a few years ago, perfecting his knowledge. It was therefore natural that when he joined the “Huang Tao” Society he was called upon to interpret for its Japanese “advisers,” chiefly “Konomi-san.”

Zung Bing, handsome and debonair, met Konomi through a Japanese friend last November. Konomi was then living in the Astor House and used the name “Tanaka,” Zung Bing told the Court. The smart young Chinese, however, soon learned Konomi’s real name. It was not long before the two got on friendly terms with each other. Already in January Konomi got Zung a pass to enter the Eastern area. Soon afterwards Konomi asked him to join the “Reformed Government,” which was in the process of being organized. The headquarters were on the sixth floor of the New Asia Hotel.

On February 3 Zung was one of many Chinese and Japanese who attended a banquet given in the New Asia in honour of Zang Nyoh-tsing (weight, 315 lb., former prisoner at the Ward Road Jail), who was to be made chairman of the “Huang Tao” Society. Zung well remembers some of the more important persons who attended this dinner. Zung further told the Court that during the first week of February he frequently saw Konomi with the object of obtaining from the Japanese “adviser” a permit for operating a gambling house in Nantao.

Editor Assassinated

Mr. Tsai Tiao-tu, the editor of a Chinese newspaper in which alleged anti-Japanese articles had appeared, was assassinated on February 5 and his head, minus the body, was found the following day in Route Stanislas Chevalier with a general warning not to engage in anti-Japanese activities. A Chinese witness described in court on Thursday how he was given the unenviable task in the New Asia Hotel, of washing the newspaper-man’s head so that it would be fit for exhibition in the French Concession. Zung Bing, in his evidence, shed further light on the murder of Tsai.

Zung Bing said he visited Konomi’s room (No. 626) in the New Asia Hotel on February 8, when the “adviser” informed him of Tsai’s death. Zung quoted Konomi as saying that he had wanted Tsai’s head to be thrown into the French Police Headquarters in Route Stanislas Chevalier to embarrass the French Police but that the presence of guards defeated this happy scheme. Konomi revealed that the editor’s head was sent to the French Concession in a motor-car.

A month later Zung Bing became a full-fledged member of an organization known as the “Asia Rehabilitation Society.” He continued to see Konomi frequently and acted as an interpreter for the “adviser” to the “Huang Tao” group. He said that as Konomi’s interpreter he heard many discussions about the butchering of Chinese bodies the heads, arms and hands of which were being placed at the time on streets in the International Settlement and French Concession or sent to prominent Chinese who were to be intimidated. He also admitted hearing frequent references to the bombing of Chinese newspapers publishing virulent anti-Japanese articles.

1938年9月10日

Konomi，化名田中，被描绘为恐怖分子的“智囊”
证人描述“黄道”社的内部运作；提及刘赫曼博士案

为准备第一特区法院对该案的下次听证，租界侦探昨天加紧了对今年以来由位于虹口新亚酒店六楼总部的亲日暴徒团伙“黄道”或“黄道”帮实施的恐怖统治的调查。该团伙中尚未入狱的成员已四散，其中主要华人头目臧念清（Zang Nyoh-tsing）已被委派离开上海，担任“沪宁及沪杭地区驻防司令”。

租界警方通缉的另一名重要人物是一名叫Konomi（未提供名字或首字母缩写）的日本人，化名田中。根据在中国法庭上提供的证词，此人有时穿着中式服装，直到去年四月第一周一直担任“黄道”社的“顾问”。周四，法庭出示了他的照片以及该组织许多其他成员的照片，并由证人进行了指认。

侦探昨天梳理的重要法庭证据中，包括一名懂日语的年轻华人Zung Bing（或Zung Ziang）提供的证词，他有力地揭示了自去年冬天成立以来该恐怖社团的内部运作情况。他的故事得到了目前被拘留的几名帮派成员证词的佐证，读起来几乎像侦探小说。

精通日语

Zung Bing告诉法庭，他在虹口一名日本医生处当学徒时学会了说日语，并于几年前访问日本，进一步完善了语言知识。因此，当他加入“黄道”社时，自然被要求为其日本“顾问”担任翻译，主要是为“Konomi先生”服务。

Zung Bing英俊潇洒，去年十一月通过一位日本朋友结识了Konomi。Zung Bing告诉法庭，Konomi当时住在礼查饭店（Astor House），并使用“田中”这个名字。然而，这位精明的年轻华人很快就知道了Konomi的真名。不久之后，两人建立了友好关系。早在今年一月，Konomi就为Zung搞到了进入东区的通行证。不久后，Konomi邀请他加入正在组建中的“维新政府”。总部设在新亚酒店六楼。

2月3日，Zung是参加在新亚酒店举行的宴会的众多中日人士之一，该宴会是为了庆祝臧念清（体重315磅，前华德路监狱囚犯）出任“黄道”社主席。Zung清楚地记得参加这次晚宴的一些重要人物。Zung还告诉法庭，在二月的第一周，他经常见到Konomi，目的是从这位日本“顾问”那里获得在南市经营赌场的许可证。

编辑遇刺

某中文报纸编辑蔡钓徒先生，该报据称刊登了反日文章，于2月5日遇刺身亡，次日其无尸头颅在斯塔尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路被发现，并附有一般性警告，告诫人们不得从事反日活动。周四在法庭上，一名中国证人描述了他是如何在新亚酒店承担这项令人不快的任务的，即清洗这位报人的头颅，以便使其适合在法租界展示。Zung Bing在其证词中进一步揭示了蔡氏被杀的真相。

Zung Bing说，他于2月8日访问了Konomi在新亚酒店的房间（626号），当时这位“顾问”通知他蔡氏已死。Zung引用Konomi的话说，他原本希望将蔡氏的头颅扔进斯塔尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路的法国警察总部，以使法国警方难堪，但由于警卫的存在，这一“妙计”未能得逞。Konomi透露，编辑的头颅是用汽车送往法租界的。

一个月后，Zung Bing成为一个名为“亚洲复兴社”的组织的正式成员。他继续经常与Konomi见面，并担任“黄道”集团“顾问”的翻译。他说，作为Konomi的翻译，他听到许多关于肢解中国尸体的讨论，这些尸体的头颅、手臂和手当时被放置在公共租界和法租界的街道上，或寄送给旨在恐吓的知名中国人。他还承认经常听到有人提及轰炸刊登激烈反日文章的中文报纸。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

SEP 1 O 1938

Those 27 Pistols Again
At the beginning of April, while discussing the terroristic activities of the "Huang Tao" Society with Konomi, Zung testified that Konomi pointed with pride to the fact that he had purchased 27 automatic pistols from the Shanghai Municipal Police through the Japanese military authorities in March. Zung exclaimed that this was foolish, but Konomi only chuckled and explained that as the pistols were being used, the identifying numbers were being filed off. Besides, he (Konomi) had written a letter to the Shanghai Municipal Police notifying them that all the pistols had been stolen. Zung stated that the following day he saw three Chinese in the process of filing numbers off pistols, in the New Asia Hotel.
Two of the 27 pistols have since been identified by arms experts as having figured in two of the assassinations ascribed to the "Huang Tao" gang. The actual date of sale by the Police to the Japanese military was March 14.
During the first week of April Konomi regretfully informed Zung that he was being relieved of his post as "adviser" to the "Huang Tao" Society, as his name had been mentioned in connection with a kidnapping for $300,000 ransom. Konomi said that his successor would be a man named Haiichi. This statement is corroborated by the testimony of several other former members of the terrorist group.
Dr. Herman Liu's Murder
Dr. Herman C. E. Liu, internationally known Chinese educator and civic leader, was assassinated by a gunman on Bubbling Well Road, at Majestic Road, on April 7 while he was waiting for an omnibus with his small son. On April 8, Zung Bing testified, Konomi showed him a clipping from a newspaper describing the crime. Zung Bing quoted Konomi as saying blandly that he had "got rid of the biggest of the anti-Japanese leaders in Shanghai."

1938年9月10日

那27支手枪再次出现
四月初，在与野村（Konomi）讨论“黄道”会的恐怖活动时，曾炳（Zung）作证说，野村自豪地指出，他已于三月通过日本军方从上海公共租界工部局警务处购买了27支自动手枪。曾炳惊呼此举愚蠢，但野村只是窃笑，并解释说，在使用这些手枪时，识别号码已被锉掉。此外，他（野村）已致函上海公共租界工部局警务处，通知他们所有手枪均已被盗。曾炳称，次日他在新亚酒店看见三名中国人正在锉除手枪上的号码。
此后，武器专家已确认，这27支手枪中的两支涉及归咎于“黄道”帮的两起暗杀案。警方将手枪出售给日本军方的实际日期为3月14日。
四月的第一周，野村遗憾地告知曾炳，他将被解除“黄道”会“顾问”一职，因为他的名字与一起索要30万美元赎金的绑架案有关。野村称，他的继任者是一个名叫海一（Haiichi，音译）的人。这一说法得到了该恐怖组织其他几名前成员的证词佐证。
刘赫曼博士遇害案
国际知名的中国教育家和社会领袖刘赫曼（Herman C. E. Liu）博士于4月7日在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）与大西路（Majestic Road）路口等待公共汽车时，与其幼子一同被一名枪手暗杀。据曾炳作证，4月8日，野村向他展示了一份描述该罪行的报纸剪报。曾炳引用野村的话说，他轻描淡写地表示已“除掉了上海最大的反日领袖”。

Subject Murder of Tsai Tiao Tu, proprietor and managing-director of
Social Evening News, whose head was found on Rue Stanislas Chevalier
on February 6, 1938.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by

With reference to the above murder, I have to
report that further information has been obtained to the
effect that the offence was attributable to the work of
certain agents of the Asia Rehabilitation Society (Recently
renamed Dah Ming Association 大民會) and one Zung Bing (陳平)
alias Zung Wen-ziang (陳文祥) who was then head of the Schem-
ing Department of the local Japanese Military Police Headquar-
ters.

In order to relate the circumstances surrounding
the murder of the said journalist, it appears advisable in
the first place to deal with the biography of Zung Bing
which is as follows:-

In his early teens Zung Bing was a regular
visitor to the N.Y.K. Mail Wharf in the Hongkew District,
seeking alms from all passengers in order to maintain a living.
It happened that a Japanese subject named Shimizu, a notor-
ious narcotic dealer, was also a regular visitor at the jetty
and consequently both had frequent interviews. Attracted
by his vivacity, Shimizu enquired into the family conditions
of Zung Bing and expressed a wish to bring him to Japan.
Zung was pleased with the proposal. Accordingly, Shimizu
deposited $30 with Zung's parents for the upkeep of the family
during their son's absence. Zung remained in Japan for a
period of 4 years and at the time of his return to the mother-
land, he was almost a naturalized Japanese and devoted his time
to building up the opium business of Shimizu.

主题：谋杀案，《社会晚报》业主兼总经理蔡钓徒（Tsai Tiao Tu）之首级于1938年2月6日在司各脱路（Rue Stanislas Chevalier）被发现。

制作人：督察顾宝华（Kuh Pao Hwa） 转呈人

关于上述谋杀案，本人须报告称，已获得进一步消息，表明该罪行系由东亚复兴会（最近更名为大民会）的某些特工以及当时担任当地日本宪兵司令部谋略部部长的曾炳（陈平），别名张文祥（Zung Wen-ziang，音译）所为。

为了叙述该记者遇害的相关情况，首先处理曾炳的生平似乎是可取的，其生平如下：

曾炳在少年时期经常出入虹口区的日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）码头，向所有乘客乞讨以维持生计。碰巧一名叫清水（Shimizu，音译）的日本籍臭名昭著的毒品贩子也经常光顾该码头，因此两人频繁接触。清水被他的活泼所吸引，询问了曾炳的家庭状况，并表示希望带他去日本。曾炳对该提议感到高兴。于是，清水向曾炳的父母存入30美元，作为其子离家期间的生活费。曾炳在日本逗留了4年，当他返回祖国时，几乎已成为归化日本人，并致力于拓展清水的鸦片生意。

Zang Moo-chang (尚慕姜), Head of the Asia
Rehabilitation Society who was then a contemporary dealing
in narcotics in the Hongkew District, once had a portion of
his opium consignment seized by the authorities. Zung
hinted to Zang through a third person that he was in a posi-
tion to arrange for the return of his cargo. As Zang was
greatly embarrassed over the seizure, he readily enlisted the
assistance of Zung who, with the help of Shimizu, eventually
succeeded in bringing about the return of the contraband.
Naturally, Zang was much obliged to Zung. Moved by the
efficiency of the youth, Zang arranged to take Zung as one of
his adopted sons. Since then, apart from assisting Shimizu
in the narcotic business, Zung worked hand-in-glove with Zang
in opium transactions, resulting in the latter pair residing
together for a period of about four years.

Some time later, opium suppression measures
were more strictly enforced locally, and all dealers in that
line became affected. Shimizu and Zang are stated to have
ceased dealing in the commodity. Zung, however, continued
to live with Zang for a further period.

Following the outbreak of the local hostilities
in 1937, Zung Bing learnt that Shimizu was connected with the
Japanese Special Service. Accordingly, he called on
Shimizu, with a view to securing a position for himself.

friend Yang Kya Kyiu was in the employ of the Japanese in Hong-
kew District, Tsai Tiao Tu should approach him and ask his
assistance. On the same evening, while Tsai Tiao Tu was at
our house, Yang happened to visit us. Tsai mentioned to Yang
about the ban on his publication and solicited his assistance
in the matter in approaching his Japanese friends. As it
seemed that Yang Kya Kyiu was on more intimate terms with me,
Tsai Tiao Tu approached me and requested me to speak favourably
on his behalf to Yang who had promised assistance in the matter.

At the request of Yang Kya Kyiu, Tsai Tiao Tu, in company
with Yang and myself, proceeded in my Morris Minor Sedan car
4483 (driven by Yang) to the New Asia Hotel, Tiendong Road,
at about 10 a.m. February 1, 1938. As Yang failed to meet his
Chinese friend in the hotel from whom he desired assistance in
the matter, we three then had tiffin there, after which we re-
turned to our home in Rue August Boppe. We then called at the
New Asia Hotel on the following two mornings, but were unsuccess-
ful in contacting Yang's friend.

Sir,

I have to report that on 6.5.1938 I received a telephone
message from a Chinese female (previously known to me as a taxi
dancer in the Ambassador Ballroom) asking if she could see me
as she had certain knowledge relating to the death of Tsah Diau
Doo (蔡釣徒) whose head was found in Frenchtown early this year.
I made an appointment with this female and received from
her certain information which was found to affect her husband
more than she. Arrangements were accordingly made and on the
evening of the 9.5.1938 she accompanied her husband Zing Sih
Kong (秦錫康) to my home where the following facts were
related by Zing.

Prior to the hostilities Zing Sih Kong owned a Casings

Zing has been residing with his concubine at No. 9 Kah Yue Li,

the newly formed 'Nanking Reformed Government'. Yang having
close connection with the Japanese and being resident at the New

proceed to the factbry. On the first occasion he accompanied
the party.

paper, 'The Social News' and was trying to re-open the press
in Foochow Road and, hearing that Zing Sih Kong had obtained a

Gruesome
Discovery
Of Murder

Head Of Director Of
Chinese Daily Is
Found In Street

One of the most gruesome dis-
coveries ever to be made in the
French Concession streets was re-
ported on Sunday night with the
finding of a chopped off head of a
Chinese lying at the foot of a cement
post, near 12 Route Stanislas Che-
valier.

On making the gruesome discovery
the police officer took the head to
the police station, where it was
examined and an immediate city-
wide search was instituted for the
body. Later the head was identified
as being that of Mr. Tsai Tio-tou,
34-year-old former manager of the
"Social Evening News."

Stuck on the post, near which the
head was found lying, was a sheet
of paper carrying a warning in
Chinese characters, "Warning To
Anti-Japanese Elements."

Police Baffled

Police were at a loss to ascertain
a motive behind the brutal killing
of Mr. Tsai, whose torso has not
been found as yet. It will be re-
called that on the evening that the
"Social Evening News" stopped
publication, on instructions from the
censorship office, its offices at 222
Shantung Road were bombed by
some terrorists.

Mr. Tsai, it is understood, had been
missing since Saturday and relatives
suspected that he had been kidnap-
ped by terrorists, who, it is also
believed, were responsible for
throwing a bomb in the offices of
the paper.

骇人听闻的
谋杀案
发现

中文日报主编之
头颅在街头
被发现

据报道，周日晚在法租界街道上发现了有史以来最骇人听闻的景象之一：一颗中国人的头颅被砍下，躺在斯坦尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路（Route Stanislas Chevalier）12号附近的一根水泥柱脚下。

警方人员在发现这一骇人景象后，将头颅带至捕房，经检查后立即在全市范围内展开搜捕以寻找尸体。随后，该头颅被确认为前《社会晚报》经理、34岁的蔡钓徒（Tsai Tio-tou）先生所有。

在发现头颅的水泥柱上贴着一张纸，上面用汉字写着一则警告：“警告反日分子。”

警方困惑不解

警方对于确定杀害蔡先生的残酷动机感到束手无策，其躯干至今尚未找到。回想起来，在《社会晚报》接到审查机构指令停刊的那个晚上，其位于山东路222号的办事处遭到了一些恐怖分子的炸弹袭击。

据悉，蔡先生自周六起一直失踪，亲属怀疑他被恐怖分子绑架，人们还认为这些恐怖分子应对向报社办公室投掷炸弹一事负责。

February 8, 1938.
Morning Translation.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao Morning Edition:

THE MURDER OF TSAI TIAO-TU

At 10.10 p.m. on February 6 a human head was discovered on the foot path by the side of electric pole No.6458 in front of House No.12 Route Stanislas Chevalier, French Concession, to the east of the Shanghai Second Special District Court. A piece of white paper on which were written the following words: "Statement Regarding Execution Of A Traitor - End Of Anti-Japanese Elements (?)" was pasted on the electric pole. A report was immediately made to the Police Station by a policeman on patrol duty and detectives were sent to the place where they removed the sheet of white paper and took away the head.

Yesterday morning the Procuratorate of the Shanghai Second Special District Court held an inquest. At about 11 a.m. Procurator Wong Zing (主任), in company with Mr. Chiang Tsing (董璿), the Court Doctor, arrived at the Dong Jen Fu Yuan Dong Benevolent Institution and as a result of an examination, the head, which was closely cropped, was found to be that of a male person of over 30 years of age and had been severed from body after death. It must have been hacked more than ten times before it came off completely from the body as there was still attached to it a piece of flesh at the back of the neck. After completing his examination of the head, the Procurator was requested to hand it over to the Municipal Hospital of the French Concession for a further examination by French doctors.

As a result of exhaustive enquiries made by our reporter at various sources yesterday afternoon, it was established that the human head was that of Tsai Tiao-tu (蔡釣徒), Managing Director of the "Social Evening News" (社會晚報), because as soon as it was brought back to the Police Station, it was identified as the head of Tsai Tiao-tu. Consequently, detectives were detailed to call at House No.7 Keng Yue Li (賡餘里), Rue Auguste Boppe, the residence of Tsai Tiao-tu, where they learned that he had not been home since February 4. Later, Tsai's sister went to the Police Station where she was shown a photograph of the head. As a result of careful examination, it was definitely established that it was the head of Tsai Tiao-tu. As the Police still require the head for a further examination, she was told to return later to remove the head for burial.

So far as this paper learns, the "Social Evening News," of which Tsai Tiao-tu was the Managing Director, has already published 1,421 issues. It was ordered to close by the S.M.C. on January 18 and as a result the "Social Morning Post" (社會晨刊), an affiliated organ of the "Social Evening News," which had only published 36 issues in all, likewise suspended publication. Following the suspension of publication by these two papers, Tsai Tiao-tu planned to resume the publication of his papers under the name of "Social News" (社會新聞) and had engaged a certain Mr. Hickey, an American citizen, to act as Manager of the publication.

《华美晚报》晨刊：

蔡钓徒谋杀案

2月6日晚上10时10分，在法租界斯坦尼斯拉斯·谢瓦利埃路12号门前、上海第二特区法院以东的第6458号电线杆旁的人行道上，发现了一颗人头。电线杆上贴着一张白纸，上面写着以下文字：“关于处决汉奸之声明 - 反日分子之终结 (?)”。一名执勤巡警立即向捕房报告，侦探被派往现场，他们取下了那张白纸并带走了头颅。

昨天上午，上海第二特区法院检察官署举行了验尸。上午11时许，主任检察官王静（Wong Zing，音译）会同法院法医蒋璟（Chiang Tsing，音译）先生到达同仁辅元堂，经检验，这颗剃得很短的头颅属于一名30多岁的男性，系死后与身体分离。由于颈部后方仍连着一块肉，头颅在被完全砍下前必定被砍了十多次。检察官完成对头颅的检查后，受请将其移交给法租界市立医院，以便法国医生进行进一步检查。

本报记者昨日下午通过多方渠道进行详尽查询后查明，这颗人头属于《社会晚报》总经理蔡钓徒（Tsai Tiao-tu），因为头颅被带回捕房后，即被确认为蔡钓徒的头颅。因此，侦探被派往赓余里7号（Keng Yue Li，Rue Auguste Boppe），即蔡钓徒的住所，得知他自2月4日起便未回家。后来，蔡的妹妹前往捕房，向她展示了头颅的照片。经仔细辨认，最终确定这确实是蔡钓徒的头颅。由于警方仍需保留头颅以供进一步检查，被告知稍后再来领取头颅进行安葬。

据本报获悉，蔡钓徒任总经理的《社会晚报》已出版1,421期。该报于1月18日被上海公共租界工部局勒令关闭，因此，《社会晚报》的附属刊物《社会晨刊》（仅出版了36期）也随即停刊。在这两份报纸停刊后，蔡钓徒计划以《社会新闻》的名义恢复出版其报纸，并聘请了一位美国公民希基（Hickey）先生担任出版经理。

With reference to the attached photostatic copy of a
note found posted on an electric light pole near the spot
where the head of Mr. Tsai Tiao Tu, former Managing-
Director of the Social Evening News, was found at 10 p.m.
February 6, 1938, an examination has been made of the
handwriting in this note, on the instructions of the A.A.
to D.C. (Special Branch), and it shows that the writer is
of Chinese nationality but possesses a poor knowledge of
the Chinese language. It is difficult to state conclusively,
whether or not, the writing was carried out in an endeavour
to disguise the hand.

It is of interest to note that prior to the closing of
the offices of the Social Evening News on December 18, 1938,
the late Tsai Tiao Tu made a statement among his friends to
the effect that he approved of the anti-Japanese elements
and he himself was of same mind as his patriotic fellow-
countrymen and in consequence he is referred to ironically
as a person with "anti-Japanese" tendencies in the epistle.

There is no record of the "Righteous Corps" with the
Special Branch and the name has never previously come to
the notice of this Branch.

Clerk Mai Yoh, attached to Crime Branch, upon being
shown the handwriting, states that the writing is that of
a low class Chinese scholar.
